text: Despite the pandemic, consider the fundamentals of growth in our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN has a growing middle class and, in fact, will be one of the parts of the world in the next 20 years with the fastest growing middle class.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also have a rapidly expanding digital economy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is no accident that we have a disproportionate number of unicorns, not just in Singapore, but also in Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and expanding across ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are also well-placed to leverage the reconfiguration of supply chains that is occurring now in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have a longstanding, strong relationship with the US.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It includes vital areas: defence, security, economic, cybersecurity and people-to-people education.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And as the digital economy grows, we should all remember that the US is home to a vast pool of innovation, technology and talent that they harvest from all over the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Its companies in Silicon Valley and beyond are global champions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It remains at the forefront of developments in science and technology.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: American companies like Pfizer and Moderna have been trailblazers on vaccines and treatments.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: American innovation and enterprise remain engines for global growth.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: American companies will continue to lead the digital revolution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is why I never count the Americans out.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Stop for a moment to think about that.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US has more invested in Southeast Asia than it has in India, China, Japan and South Korea combined.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Every time I met President Trump, I reminded him of this statistic.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, you understand then why our relationship with the US remains crucial.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And the US military presence has underpinned peace and stability in our region for over half a century.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I recently spoke separately with newly-appointed US Secretary of State Antony Blinken and the National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have known them in various incarnations before their current positions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We reaffirmed our excellent relationship and robust cooperation and discussed doing more in areas like global health, cybersecurity and the digital economy so that together, we can better tackle the challenges of our generation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With China, we share a deep, historical, cultural, linguistic legacy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have a wide-ranging and important relationship, and I will get Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat to speak more about that after this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I want to highlight a few points.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have three government-to-government projects: the Suzhou Industrial Park, the Tianjin Eco City and Chongqing Connectivity Initiative and all these have made commendable progress over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And you will know that Deputy Prime Minister Heng just co-chaired the Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Despite the pandemic, we have kept up our pace of cooperation and engagement with China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We sent medical equipment and supplies to each other at crucial stages of the crisis respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For operational reasons, I cannot go into details but let me assure you – when the chips were down on either side – fortunately, at different times – we stepped up and we helped.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Politburo Member Yang Jiechi visited Singapore last August and I also met State Councillor and Foreign Minister Wang Yi during his transit in Singapore in October.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Needless to say, I have been on the phone with him several times in the last year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Going forward, we will continue to strengthen existing collaboration, with Singapore plugged into China's dual-circulation strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we will look for new opportunities and break new ground.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, given our deep friendships and our investments with both the US and China, it is inevitable that we will feel the tug of great power competition from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must not be upset or panic whenever we feel these tugs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, I would say this is a design feature of the way we engage the two superpowers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is normal for two superpowers to try to influence others to their way of thinking, particularly, if we are considered to be an important account, worth pushing and pulling.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I want to stress it is normal – in fact, it is imperative – for Singapore, or for any country, for that matter, to want to be able to choose for ourselves instead of being forced into making decisions by other people – in other words, not to be forced into making invidious choices.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, in navigating between the two superpowers, we must continue to maintain a consistent and principled foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For me, in simple terms, it means, I say the same thing to Wang Yi as I say to Antony Blinken.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I do not have the luxury of saying different things to both of them and then hoping they do not compare notes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Next, we exercise our sovereign rights but with full respect for a rules-based multilateral world order and international law, and regardless of inducements or threats.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What that means is that from time to time, we will have to say "no" to one or the other or both.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When that happens – if you look back over the last five years, there have been incidents.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We depend on the confidence, cohesion and unity of the Singaporean public and of Members of this House, across party lines, to stick together.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That is how we maintain our relevance and our strategic autonomy and that is how we preserve our independence and our unique identity as a multi-racial, multicultural city state in the heart of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: By being relevant to both and at the same time, making it very clear to both of them that we will never be a stalking horse or a Trojan Horse for the other.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This same principle actually applies in our dealings with our closest neighbours, which I think Miss Rachel Ong and others have asked about.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With Malaysia, we have always sought a win-win approach in the many areas where we have common interests.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I had previously spoken about how we had helped to bring each other's citizens home – I told Minister Hishammuddin we "tumpang" each other's transport – and we facilitated travel between our countries for those with urgent and compassionate needs because so many of us have relatives across the Causeway.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have coordinated well with Malaysia on our COVID-19 safeguards in order to minimise the disruptions to our companies, workers and citizens as well as the cross-border flow of goods and supplies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Foreign Minister Hishammuddin Hussein is a good friend whom I have known for two decades now.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We met at the Causeway but with the boundary separating us on 26 July last year to discuss our travel arrangements in light of the border closures.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to work with Malaysia to gradually resume the cross-border movement of people, but this will need to include mutually agreed public health protocols to preserve the public health and safety of our peoples, while taking into account the medical resources available on both sides.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I will continue to maintain regular communication with both the Foreign Minister Hishammuddin and the Menteri Besar of Johor Hasni Mohammad.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have managed to make progress on bilateral projects and issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When completed, the RTS Link will ease Causeway congestion, improve connectivity and foster more convenient people-to-people ties and generate shared economic and social benefits.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Where we have had differences, we have also been able to manage them in a calm and rational way.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We had been flexible in trying to work out an arrangement that was acceptable to both sides and had agreed to suspend the construction of the HSR Project in September 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And then, in May 2020, we agreed to extend the suspension period to 31 December 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However – and I think Minister Ong has explained to this House before – we could not accept Malaysia's latest HSR proposal as it constituted a fundamental departure from our prior agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ultimately, whilst we seek cooperation with our neighbours, we must always ensure that Singapore's long-term interests and rights are also protected.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Still, it is good that both sides have been able to handle this amicably and will continue cooperation in other areas.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In Malaysia, Movement Control Orders have also been implemented in the different states.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Malaysia declared a State of Emergency which will last until August 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both the pandemic and the political situation will remain fluid and we probably will see an election in Malaysia later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Regardless of the outcome, we continue to look for opportunities to work with Malaysia and to make progress where we can.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On Indonesia, we continue to have a close and substantive partnership, even more so during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: High-level exchanges have continued, including Foreign Minister Retno Marsudi's recent visit to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, I have been in almost daily contact with her, either by phone or via WhatsApp message for quite some time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to work together towards a strong recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Areas for cooperation between Singapore and Indonesia include public health, economic growth and investments, financial cooperation and safe travel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There has already been progress on some of these areas.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I will just give you a quick few examples.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee and President Joko Widodo endorsed the renewal of our Bilateral Financial Arrangement in 2020, which will help support monetary and financial stability in both our countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also launched an RGL with Indonesia in October 2020 to keep up business activities and people-to-people exchanges in a safe way.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Whilst this Reciprocal Green Lane is currently suspended, we look forward to working with Indonesia to resume this when both sides are ready to do so, when the pandemic is under better control.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also been providing medical supplies, including diagnostic test kits, PCR machines and personal protective equipment (PPE) to both the central and regional governments as well as various non-governmental organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In addition, we have taken steps on outstanding bilateral issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I am pleased that officials on both sides have continued discussions to move these issues forward.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It speaks to the strength of our relationship that though the current situation may be challenging, we continue to look for ways to work constructively together.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is our way of fulfilling Deputy Prime Minister Heng's challenge of emerging stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will emerge stronger in an uncertain world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While the situation in Singapore has improved greatly since last year, normalcy remains some way off.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Meanwhile, MFA will have to maintain and strengthen relations with our neighbours and partners to achieve peace and prosperity for ourselves and our region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Minister Balakrishnan has said earlier, as a responsible member of the international community, we worked with our partners to bring Singaporeans home and helped foreign nationals do likewise, despite the global impact of travel restrictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We kept supply chains open and served as an airbridge to facilitate critical and compassionate travel and the operations of United Nation (UN) agencies such as the World Health Organization and UNICEF.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a reliable host, we saw to the welfare of vulnerable foreigners working in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We ensured medical care, meals and phonecards for migrant workers and mandated that their salaries be paid on time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our relations with our immediate neighbours, Malaysia and Indonesia, remain strong.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While issues have cropped up from time to time, we have addressed them constructively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We should not take this cooperation for granted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Relations with our nearest neighbour, Malaysia, can be best characterised by the Malay saying “bagai aur dengan tebing” or like bamboo and the water’s edge.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Malaysia and Singapore are deeply intertwined, with strong people-to-people and economic linkages.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Although COVID-19 and the ensuing border restrictions have caused significant disruptions, both countries have cooperated to alleviate these challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the early days of COVID-19, we appreciated Prime Minister Muhyiddin’s assurance that supplies from Malaysia would not be disrupted even with their lockdown.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Minister Vivian Balakrishnan earlier said, Singapore and Malaysia have helped each other during this difficult time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, in April 2020, we brought 60 Malaysians out from Bangladesh on a Singapore Airlines flight.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Malaysia also helped Singaporeans return home, including 22 Singaporeans who left Nepal the same month on a Malaysian government flight.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also worked very closely with Malaysian authorities to facilitate Singaporeans’ travel into Malaysia for essential and compassionate reasons.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since March 2020, we have also facilitated the appeals of more than 250 Singaporean citizens and Permanent Residents to travel to Malaysia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When Malaysia implemented its Movement Control Order in March 2020, many Malaysians who used to commute to work in Singapore daily could not do so at that time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We worked with employers on short-term housing for these workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In August 2020, we launched the Periodic Commuting arrangement to facilitate cross-border travel for work.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have kept up momentum on our bilateral projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will now elaborate on these relationships in Malay.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):    Mr Zhulkarnain has asked how we have maintained close ties with our nearest neighbour Malaysia, during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly given the disruptions to cross-border flows.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has brought sharp focus to the interdependence of both countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have worked closely with the Perikatan Nasional government to tackle the effects of COVID-19, especially on essential cross-border movements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This allowed us to ensure that our supply chains with Malaysia continued uninterrupted, particularly for perishable food products, despite the border restrictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Just like us, Malaysia has been working hard to bring its COVID-19 situation under control.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Various categories of Movement Control Orders (MCOs) have been implemented in the different states in Malaysia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Malaysia also declared a State of Emergency in January 2021.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We wish them well and stand ready to provide any assistance that might be needed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Throughout the pandemic, our leaders and civil services have maintained good, open lines of communication.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has changed the mode of our interactions with Malaysian leaders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Nevertheless, we have adopted other ways to continue these high-level interactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This has allowed us to cooperate constructively in facing the challenges posed by the pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I would also like to put on record Singapore’s appreciation for Malaysia’s successful APEC Chairmanship despite COVID-19, capped off by Malaysia’s successful hosting of the virtual APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in November 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such interactions continue to advance regional economic integration even as we tackle the pandemic together.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Now allow me to turn to Singapore’s relationship with Indonesia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our relationship with Indonesia is deep and multifaceted, with mutually beneficial collaboration spanning trade, investment, tourism, security, and education sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have worked well with President Joko Widodo and his Administration and look forward to sustaining this positive momentum.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also maintained close regional engagement with Indonesia’s provincial leaders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Prior to the onset of the pandemic, I made a working visit to several cities in the Indonesian provinces, including Jambi City, Pekanbaru, and Batam.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This was part of our overall effort to strengthen cooperation with Indonesia’s regions and suss out new opportunities for collaboration.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore looks forward to continuing our strong links with the regional leaders and hopes to restart exchanges through physical visits when the situation allows.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Joan Pereira has pointed out the substantive cooperation between Indonesia and Singapore in many different areas and enquired about our efforts to further strengthen this relationship during this COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have kept up our high-level exchanges with Indonesia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many of our Cabinet Ministers and officials kept up regular engagements and communication with their counterparts through video and phone calls.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the strategic level, we have continued discussions on the management of our Flight Information Region (FIR) and military training with Indonesia separately but concurrently under the Framework for Discussions announced at the Leaders’ Retreat in 2019.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our defence and security establishments continue to maintain strong ties and stand ready to work together in areas such as counterterrorism.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also working closely to tackle common challenges such as in the environment sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Following its launch, the RGL successfully facilitated official and business travel.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While currently suspended, we will continue working with Indonesia to resume the RGL when both sides are ready to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a concerned neighbour, we have contributed in our own small ways to Indonesia’s fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the early days of the pandemic, we conveyed medical supplies, including PCR machines and test kits, and PPEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain has also asked for an update on our relationship with Brunei.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We enjoy a longstanding special relationship built on a strategic trust long forged between Singapore and Brunei.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This trust is evidenced by, among others, our strong defence cooperation and the Currency Interchangeability Agreement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore is one of Brunei’s main export destinations and main sources of imports.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore and Brunei also recently signed Memorandums of Understanding to cooperate on social development in September 2020, and on agri-food and agro-technology cooperation in February 2021.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: DPM Heng Swee Keat and I visited Brunei in November 2020 to offer condolences on behalf of the Singapore Government on the passing of His Majesty the Sultan’s son, His Royal Highness Prince Haji ‘Abdul ‘Azim.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This was the first overseas visit by Singapore political office holders since COVID-19 travel restrictions were imposed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have always enjoyed strong cooperation with Brunei in various sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have leveraged our strong ties to address the challenges posed by COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This includes the launch of the RGL between Singapore and Brunei on 1 September 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore has also unilaterally opened our borders to travellers from Brunei.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore and Brunei will continue to explore cooperation in new areas, including agri-food, agro-technology, and climate change.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These are just some ways for us to tap on the strength of our relationship with Brunei and build new avenues of cooperation in the years to come.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will strongly support Brunei in its role as ASEAN Chairman this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): We have received several questions on ASEAN.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim has asked about enhancing relations among ASEAN countries, the reputation of ASEAN in the international community, and ASEAN’s efforts on the situation in the South China Sea (SCS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Murali Pillai has asked how MFA can enhance cooperation with other countries, including ASEAN members, and about the integration of ASEAN markets, and how such efforts will improve the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A stable ASEAN is important for our development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN member states have drawn closer through COVID-19 initiatives and regional economic recovery efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Brunei’s Chairmanship of ASEAN this year aims to ramp up relations among ASEAN member states, at the NGO and the people sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, Brunei is leading efforts to establish a platform for the people of ASEAN to contribute to disaster relief efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore will work closely with Brunei on these initiatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since its establishment, ASEAN has steadily built up a reputation as a regional architecture for external powers to dialogue with member states and one another to help foster regional peace and security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have had many video conference meetings with external partners in 2020 at the ministerial level and at the leaders’ level, which will continue this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will encourage greater trade flows and open new opportunities for our businesses and our people.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is timely as we move ahead to secure our recovery from the economic impact of COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN has a role in preserving peace and stability in our region, including the South China Sea.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Despite the challenges posed by COVID-19, dialogue between ASEAN and China is on-going.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to defend our right to freedom of navigation and overflight and work through ASEAN towards an effective and substantive COC that is in accordance with universally recognised principles of international law, including the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While the pandemic has disrupted connectivity among ASEAN member states, we will encourage ASEAN member states to cooperate on post-pandemic recovery, regional supply chain connectivity, safely restoring cross-border travel and enhancing resilience against public health emergencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Just as the Prime Minister encouraged countries to cooperate and develop a system to verify COVID-19 tests and vaccinations, I hope ASEAN will cooperate on measures to safely restore regional connectivity when conditions permit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN has made steady progress combating the pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It promptly set up the ASEAN Coordinating Council Working Group on Public Health Emergencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This led to several initiatives including the COVID-19 ASEAN Response Fund.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore recognises the importance of these mechanisms, which have enhanced our ability collectively to deal with COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Derrick Goh has asked how Singapore can support this year’s ASEAN Chair, Brunei, to forge a closer ASEAN.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore supports Brunei’s Chairmanship agenda and will work with Brunei to advance ASEAN community building, economic integration and regional stability, and to develop cooperation in new areas of importance such as digitalisation, cybersecurity, smart cities and climate change.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As ASEAN-EU Country Coordinator, we have also strengthened cooperation between ASEAN and the European Union or EU following the recent elevation of dialogue relations to a Strategic Partnership.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: An ASEAN-EU FTA would present new opportunities for inter-regional collaboration on issues such as supply chain and digital connectivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to the finalisation of the ASEAN-EU FTA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Abdul Samad has asked how we are deepening our engagement with other key partners beyond ASEAN.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: India and Singapore must continue to collaborate on new frontiers such as innovation, the digital economy and FinTech.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore was among the largest foreign investors in India for the past several years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, Novade is a start-up providing smart field management solutions for CapitaLand and local developers in India’s construction industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And this industry contributed over US$188 billion to India’s GDP in FY2019 and is expected to be the world’s third largest construction market by 2024.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to collaborating with India in other areas of mutual interest, including digital connectivity and artificial intelligence, as well as facilitate our companies’ effort at harnessing the huge Indian market.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Singapore assumes the Coordinatorship of ASEAN-India Dialogue relations in August 2021, we will seek to promote win-win cooperation between ASEAN and India.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked when our citizens will be able to travel to perform the Haj and Umrah.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We understand that our Muslim community longs to perform the Haj and Umrah.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MFA will work closely with MOH and MUIS to monitor the COVID-19 situation and assess when it would be safe for such travel to resume, in line with the overall national advisory for overseas travel.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We seek the community’s continued understanding and patience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will support our companies as they explore opportunities in the Middle East’s largest economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also welcome recent positive developments in the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Alex Yam has noted Israel and a number of Arab countries have normalised relations following the signing of the Abraham Accords in August 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In January, Qatar and its neighbours agreed to restore ties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that these developments lead to new opportunities for cooperation and growth, and sustainable peace and stability in the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We continue to encourage Israel and the Palestinians to resolve their long-standing conflict.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore has taken a consistent and principled position, supporting a negotiated two-state solution consistent with the relevant United Nations Security Council Resolutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The continent is the fastest urbanising region in the world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Its young population has the potential to unlock significant economic growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Joan Pereira has asked how Singaporean companies are tapping the continent’s market.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There are currently about 60 Singapore companies operating across Sub-Saharan Africa in a wide range of sectors such as agri-business, oil and gas, and FinTech.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One such company is Ascent Solutions, which specialises in the Internet of Things or "IoT" and GPS Security Tracking Solutions for the logistics industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Its iSPOT Electronic Cargo Tracking System, for example, is deployed in several countries including Ghana, Kenya and Tanzania.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In Ghana, the National Petroleum Authority (NPA) has implemented iSPOT to track the delivery of petroleum products to 4,000 petrol retail outlets nationwide.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Africa now contributes more than 20% of Ascent’s revenue.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh has asked about our efforts to deepen our engagement in emerging markets including through measures such as the FTAs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have continued to pursue opportunities with emerging markets, including in Central and Eastern Europe, and Latin America, in areas including innovation, digitalisation and agri-food.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, we welcomed the first shipment of eggs from Poland in June 2020 as part of a larger food diversification initiative.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to the successful completion of the Eurasian Economic Union-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (EAEUSFTA), which will facilitate increased economic exchanges with the EAEU Member States Russia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, as well as the region as a whole.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will create diverse economic opportunities for Singaporean businesses in the combined Eurasian market of more than 180 million people.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also deepening our engagement with Latin America.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are currently negotiating the Pacific Alliance-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (PASFTA) and the MERCOSUR-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (MSFTA).

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are keeping up with the momentum so that we can conclude the negotiations and sign the PASFTA this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Once concluded, the PASFTA will establish the Pacific Alliance’s first FTA with Singapore, and our first bilateral FTA with Colombia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore will become the first Associate State of the Pacific Alliance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will provide Singapore a platform to pursue more economic collaboration with the Pacific Alliance, in areas such as the digital economy, trade facilitation, energy sector and infrastructure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Likewise, we hope to expeditiously conclude our FTA negotiations with MERCOSUR, which is made up of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Once concluded, these trade agreements will deepen our economic links with Latin America and strengthen Singapore’s value as a commercial bridge between Latin America and Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, I conclude by reiterating that despite the constraints imposed by COVID-19, we must continue cooperating with our partners for the security, peace, and prosperity of Singapore and the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As our external environment remains in flux, our tenacity and resilience as a people have enabled us to strengthen these relationships and advance forward.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In so doing, we strengthen Singapore’s resilience and relevance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As long as we remain relevant to the world, we secure the interests of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will turn the floor to my colleague, Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: US investments and US companies create many jobs in finance, insurance, manufacturing, technology and other sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Cooperation with the US is critical to maintaining our defence capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: President Biden is familiar with Singapore, and keen to work with us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked about the state of our relations with China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In 2020, we celebrated the 30th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Despite the pandemic, we have kept up our exchanges and cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Over the past decades, our cooperation with China has continued to progress, and developed in a way that meets China’s developmental priorities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In the process, Singapore has contributed to and benefitted from China’s growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Looking ahead, we will continue to strengthen our cooperation with China and create development opportunities for Singaporean enterprises and our workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked what are the opportunities for Singaporean businesses in China at the provincial level, and how RCEP could further boost bilateral trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With our strong historical and people-to-people links with China, Singapore is in a good position to build bridges with China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, our value proposition must go beyond our ability to speak Mandarin or understand Chinese culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These are useful to build connections with our Chinese counterparts, but there are already more than a billion people who speak Mandarin and understand Chinese culture in China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is therefore not an area where Singapore can add value to China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our value proposition lies in our ability to continuously improve, innovate, manage our economy and society well, and to be an exceptional country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In fact, it is precisely because Singapore and China are similar in some aspects, but different in others, that there are more opportunities for both sides to learn from each other, and there is greater room for us to exchange views and cooperate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: What is important is that we can seek common ground despite differences in some areas, and work together in areas of shared interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For instance, Lianhe Zaobao has a strong following in China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Chinese readers find Zaobao accessible and familiar, but its value comes from the fact that it is a Singapore newspaper and not a Chinese publication.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So it analyses global and regional developments from a Singaporean perspective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is also important that we do not take our excellent bilateral relations for granted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We should regularly renew and deepen our friendship to build on the strong foundations that our forefathers have put in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Every generation will need to invest in strengthening our relationship, strengthen mutual trust, and continually identify areas of mutually beneficial cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore’s foreign policy has always been guided by our national interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We work hard to be friends and maintain good ties with all countries, in order to preserve and enhance our security, economic and international space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, it is inevitable that our positions on various issues may differ from those of our partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This includes our neighbouring countries, as well as the US, the EU, China, Japan, India, etc.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our relations with other countries will therefore have their ups and downs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: When our relations with other countries are good, we will build on the momentum and strengthen our collaborations and friendship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, we must be prepared that countries will disagree with each other on certain issues based on different national interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The key is to find suitable platforms to resolve these disagreements in an amicable manner, by engaging with each other constructively and where possible, coming to mutually acceptable compromises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Sometimes, we may have to agree to disagree, but we can still maintain friendly relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Former Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr George Yeo had used the Taiji analogy of “zhan” to characterise Singapore-China relations; I think this is a good metaphor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: There will be some back and forth in the interactions, and some ups and downs along the way, but the two parties should remain in contact and stay engaged with each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, please allow me to continue in English.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked how Singaporeans can play their part on foreign policy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Don Wee asked about maintaining Singapore's relevance in the international community, while Mr Gerald Giam raised our technical assistance to developing countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Singapore's survival is intrinsically linked to regional and international peace and stability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Through these initiatives, we had been able to grow our international network of friends whilst reinforcing Singapore's relevance as a constructive and responsible member of the international community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These friendships, built over many years, have been especially important during times of crisis like the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: During the pandemic, our officers went beyond the call of duty to assist fellow Singaporeans in distress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Just across the Causeway, some Singaporeans were unable to make it back home following the Malaysian Movement Control Order (MCO) in March 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Some of our children were in the care of their grandparents, their guardians in Malaysia at that time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Merchor was a wonderful friend to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I also thank all our HCGs around the world for their devoted service to Singapore and Singaporeans, especially over the past year during the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I share these examples to illustrate how our MFA officers, including those serving at our overseas Missions, are frontline workers, are frontline warriors in the fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They have worked under challenging conditions to bring our citizens home and ensure that no Singaporean is left behind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They bravely continue to perform their duties to serve Singapore and Singaporeans out at post.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: On behalf of all Singaporeans, I want to thank our MFA officers for their service during this especially difficult year and also my sincere thanks to their families for their unwavering support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Your tenacity and dedication in performing your duty to the nation despite the risk to your own lives, showcase the very best of the Singapore spirit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It shows the world why we are called Singapura – a city of lion-hearted people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, in the face of global uncertainty and upheaval, domestic resilience and national unity are crucial.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The support of our people gives us strength.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The pursuit of our national interests guides our direction and the well-being of Singapore and Singaporeans is why MFA and our officers continue to brave the odds and go the extra mile to get our job done.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The Minister earlier described with great depth how we are coping with great power contestation at the Government and diplomatic levels.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: However, could I seek the Minister's view on how we can do more at the people level to strengthen our local resilience and further the understanding of our foreign policy positions as various other countries seek to steer local sentiment through either soft power projection or influence and disinformation campaigns.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Alex Yam for that very salient question.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The first point I would make is I hope they all listened to Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat's speech just now.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope it will be translated into English as well and that The Straits Times will carry it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I remind my staff that right now, actually, we are in a sweet spot, in terms of our relationship with both superpowers.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would remind Members to recall the advice that whenever we receive a message or a video, or a social media posting, always ask who does it ultimately originate from; first question.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Third question, who benefits or loses from the perspective that is being advocated from that posting?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Fourth, what are the long-term national interests of Singapore?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I am always reminded of some very good pithy and sometimes, the prickly advice that Dr Goh Keng Swee gave us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In 1970, when he was describing the difference between conducting business and conducting foreign policy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Allow me to quote just a couple of sentences from him.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: He said, "In the nature of things, relations between independent sovereign states cannot be conducted on the basis of supplicant and overlord.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The methods that are found so successful in business   these methods are not available to us as a Government." And I think that reminder is still salient after 50 years.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I hope that the people of Singapore will understand and take it in our stride.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When relations become a bit prickly, a bit uncomfortable and we go through the inevitable episodes from time to time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And Senior Minister of State Chee's reminder that our value, our unique selling point, is not to be a vassal state or to be bought or intimidated or to be a pale imitation of a larger power, but to be ourselves – authentic, reliable, trustworthy, relevant and useful – and the Member's point therefore that we need to continue to conduct foreign policy at home and to make these points to our own people and to convince them accordingly.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I have two clarifications to the Minister for Foreign Affairs about COVAX.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second clarification is, earlier during the MINDEF Committee of Supply, we were actually distributed a map showing vaccines approved around the world for use.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And I think the Minister for Defence's point was that these distribution relationships do reflect a certain power play in some traditional alliances.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister to confirm that countries joining COVAX actually, they do not have any prohibition on continuing to reach such bilateral arrangements for COVID-19 vaccine purchases, and whether he sees that these bilateral arrangements outside of COVAX will be one of the biggest challenges for the COVAX programme to succeed?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for these two salient questions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And allow me to take a step back and explain first the rationale behind COVAX.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because, in fact, this is a unique moment in public health.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Never before in history have so many vaccine candidates been developed, tested approved and deployed within one year.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It was essential, however, to have this because of the speed in which the global pandemic was galloping through the entire world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At the beginning, in fact, even, I would say right up to about September or October last year, it was not possible to be scientifically sure which one would work and the first vaccine candidate that work would not necessarily be the best.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It means when you are not certain which horse is going to reach the finish line, never mind which one is going to win, which horse is going to meet the finish line, you need to put some advance bets.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is not really about horse racing bets.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But you are putting money on the line so that multiple pharmaceutical companies would be incentivised to develop vaccines at a pace and with significant business risk.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And if there was not such a facility to pool risk, and therefore incentivise this simultaneous rapid development of vaccines, we would not be in this happy situation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Risk pooling because you do not know which vaccine will work.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second dimension of risk pooling is that some countries, have the wherewithal, and many countries do not.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the case of a pandemic, if you just split the world on the basis of "can afford" and "cannot afford", you will actually end up with more dangerous world because the virus does not respect race, language, religion, socio-economic status, wealth or lack thereof of your country.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the second dimension of COVAX risk pooling is to make sure that at least for essential personnel and the people at greatest risk across the world, there would be some vaccines available to them.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We would put money into the pot and say, "Well, there is money available, please commercial companies go and develop vaccines." And then, when we put money into the pot, although we would be entitled to our fair share on the basis of full market price, a significant amount actually would be committed to help support the less well-off countries.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I have taken some pains to explain COVAX, so that you understand it is all about risk pooling across different vaccine candidates and across different countries.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Specifically for us, apart from being one of the early birds who actually put real resources down, and I am glad that in this case, I assume that this entire House, including the Opposition, supports the Government's decisions on making advance commitments for the purchase of vaccines.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have not specifically asked for it to be earmarked for ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For ASEAN, we separately have an COVID-19 ASEAN Response Fund.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have also put money into it and that we will use on a needs basis within the ASEAN family.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I agree with your sentiment that we do need to look after our region and I hope you agree with the way which we are doing it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Over and above our contribution to the COVID-19 ASEAN Response Fund, you will also recall earlier in my speech, I mentioned that we had separately been giving test kids, PCR machines, PPE and other donations centrally, regional governments, NGOs throughout our region.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: To be honest, we have not beat our drums about it, it has been that good work has been done and it has been appreciated by our neighbours.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Rest assured, this is just another example of the way we conduct foreign policy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We cannot be bought, we cannot be bullied, we cannot be intimidated into either approving or disapproving any vaccine.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will make decisions on the basis of health and science.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But precisely because people know that is the way we decide, you will realise we become a rather important reference customer.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, there will be pressure on us, there will be push and pulls, but we must conduct this just like another example of foreign policy in a principled manner.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Chairman, I have a clarification for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I appreciate the Minister's remarks in response to the violence in Myanmar yesterday, including stating that Singapore is appalled at the use of lethal force against unarmed civilians.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Can I ask the Minister if he will be communicating these sentiments directly to the military leaders in Myanmar to emphasise our concern about the escalation of violence and to urge them to return to the negotiating table with the democratically elected civilian authorities?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Alex Yam, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: This was in reference to our place in the world when he made these remarks at the Commonwealth Conference.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Gratitude to Minister, Second Minister and Senior Minister of State Chee, as well as all our Foreign Service Officers for flying our flag high.
